Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires are marching toward the center of the park, and we can see the young Proteas in a huddle near the boundary fence. It looks like skipper Muhammad Bulbulia has a few last words to his teammates before they disperse to take their fielding positions. Viran Chamuditha and Dimantha Mahavithana will open the innings for Sri Lanka Under-19. JJ Basson has the new ball in hand and is raring to start off with two slips in place. Away we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Pitch favouring spinners - However, now things will be interesting as the pitch is surely reactive to spinners, like we have witnessed in the first inning. But if the Proteas pacers somehow pick a couple of breakthroughs in the first Powerplay, the Lankan batters would feel the heat. The openers need to address it slowly and steadily before getting aggressive. So stick around with us, refill your snacks, and join us in a bit as the second essay will commence in a few moments.

Centurion Jorich van Schalkwyk is up for a chat - Jorich says that he and his partner had a chat that if it's there, they will put it away. Adds that it was good to get a few away early, and they got off to a good start. Mentions that he loves batting with Adnaan, he is the one who goes on the attack more. Says that the wicket was a bit challenging, there was bounce, turn, but he feels they finished well after those wickets in the middle. Ends by saying that they have a good score on the board and they will try their best to defend it.

Van Schalkwyk's ton powers SA - After the fall of the third wicket, Jorich and Mbatha built a decent partnership of 48 runs. Just as the Proteas were attempting to accelerate the score, the Lankans struck back with another wicket. Despite this, Jorich showcased his resilience, eventually scoring an important century. Just after reaching this milestone, he received the green light to take on the bowlers more aggressively. However, Akash managed to dismiss him before he could become too dangerous. The lower middle order of the Proteas stepped up, forming small partnerships that ultimately contributed to a total of 261 runs.

Openers shine, but Lankan spinners turn the tide -  South Africa had 'the perfect start' from their opener, Jorich van Schalkwyk and Adnaan Lagadien. Both of them stole the show as the game progressed, building a strong partnership of 96 runs. However, it was Vigneshwaran Akash who turned the tide by breaking that partnership and taking the crucial wicket of the opposition skipper Muhammad Bulbulia. Following this, the spinners ramped up the pressure on the young Proteas, claiming another wicket. Suddenly, South Africa found themselves in a precarious position, slipping from 96 for no loss to 125-3.

The tug of war - Wow, what an inning it was! After the first half of the inning, we all thought that South Africa Under-19 have a very good chance to post a total over 300, but the Lankan bowlers came back pretty well to close things off. The Proteas have ended the inning with 261 runs on the board and Jorich van Schalkwyk was surely their standout batter, scoring 116 off 130 balls. But we also have another star player from Sri Lanka's camp and that is Vigneshwaran Akash, who just missed his five-fer by a wicket, but his contribution was more than effective for the side.

A couple of runs to end the innings! Rasith Nimsara goes full again and on middle and leg. Michael Kruiskamp heaves it off the inside half of the bat towards deep square leg and rushes back for the second run. South Africa Under-19 finish on 261/7!

Jorich van Schalkwyk and Adnaan Lagadien are the two openers for South Africa Under-19. Sri Lanka Under-19 going with spin straightaway as Viran Chamuditha has the new ball in hand. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start of the match, but before that, the players from both sides come out to the middle and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Sri Lanka's first followed by that of South Africa.

Pitch Report - Rohan Gavaskar is pitchside. He says that the sun is out, there is no chance of rain, and it is perfect weather for a cricket game. Ed Rainsford joins him and says that the pitch has dried up a lot and he is expecting the batters to have a say. Mentions that the seamers have dominated here, and India scored over 350 runs in the last game. Says that the weather has made the outfield quicker, but spinners might get some help here as well.

The captain of Sri Lanka Under-19 - Vimath Dinsara says that they would have bowled first anyway. Adds that the pitch looks different from the one they played against Namibia earlier in the tournament. Adds that they have a slim chance of qualifying, but they are not taking any extra pressure. Says that they won the last game against the Afghans and will look to do more of the same here. Informs that they have made one change as Kugathas Mathulan misses out and Vigneshwaran Akash comes in the team.

The skipper of South Africa Under-19 - Muhammad Bulbulia says that they will look to put runs on the board and hopefully defend it, as he expects the pitch to slow down and favour the spinners later on. Adds that they have had a lot of positives, especially individual gains, but unfortunately, they could not perform collectively. Ends by saying that he hopes that the players can take this into bigger and better things.

Sri Lanka Under-19 (Playing XI) - Dimantha Mahavithana, Viran Chamuditha, Senuja Wekunagoda, Vimath Dinsara (C), Kavija Gamage, Chamika Heentigala, Dulnith Sigera, Chamarindu Nethsara (WK), Sethmika Seneviratne, Rasith Nimsara and Vigneshwaran Akash (In place of Kugathas Mathulan).

South Africa Under-19 (Playing XI) - Adnaan Lagadien (In place of Armaan Manack), Jorich van Schalkwyk, Muhammad Bulbulia (C), Jason Rowles, Bandile Mbatha (In place of Bayanda Majola), Paul James, Lethabo Phahlamohlaka (WK), Corne Botha (In place of Daniel Bosman), Michael Kruiskamp (In place of Ntandoyenkosi Soni), JJ Basson and Enathi Khitshini.
TOSS - Up goes the coin and it falls in favour of the young Proteas. South Africa Under-19 have elected to BAT first.

Lankan Lion on the prowl - Sri Lanka enters this match with significant momentum after a clinical four-wicket victory over Afghanistan, proving they can handle the pressure of the Super 6s. Their campaign has been defined by balanced performances and the emergence of genuine match-winners like Viran Chamuditha, who has contributed significantly with both bat and ball, including a stunning 192-run knock earlier in the tournament. They are sitting third with four points but Afghanistan and West Indies also have the same points. Captain Vimath Dinsara has also been a pillar of stability in the middle order, while Rasith Nimsara has led the pace attack effectively with 6 wickets. With their tournament lives on the line, the Lankans will be leaning heavily on these key performers to secure the vital points needed to leapfrog their rivals in the standings. So, will South Africa Under-19 be able to end their campaign with a smile, or will Sri Lanka Under-19 ride on their momentum? Stick around to find the answers. Toss and team updates in your way.

Young Proteas' rollercoaster ride - The young Proteas have had a tournament of extreme highs and lows. While they recently made headlines by smashing a record-breaking 397/5 against Tanzania, the highest score of the tournament so far, their form in the Super 6 stage has faltered, including a tough recent loss to Australia where their batting collapsed for just 118. Despite the team's struggles, Jason Rowles has been a standout star of the campaign, sitting near the top of the run-scoring charts with 275 runs, including a magnificent 125*. On the bowling front, JJ Basson has been their primary weapon, consistently picking up wickets with an impressive tally of 9 scalps throughout the competition.

Hello and welcome, folks - The time has come where we shift our focus to an intriguing Super 6 encounter at the Queens Sports Club in Bulawayo. In this eighth match of the Super 6 stage, South Africa takes on Sri Lanka in a contest that carries vastly different stakes for both sides. While the tournament has reached a boiling point for some, this specific fixture represents a dead rubber for South Africa, who have unfortunately fallen out of semi-final contention. Conversely, for Sri Lanka, the pressure is at an absolute maximum, this is a must-win game to keep their hopes of reaching the final four alive in a tightly contested Group 1.

Match intro - As the ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup 2026 shifts into the business end of the high-stakes Super 6 phase, Match 8 presents a mouth-watering clash between two sides with high aspirations - South Africa Under-19 and Sri Lanka Under-19. With the semi-final spots looming, this encounter at the Queens Sports Club in Bulawayo could very well define the trajectory for both teams in the tournament. South Africa - The young Proteas enter this match looking to reclaim their status as a global powerhouse but with no points to their name in the Super 6s phase, they will be under pressure to perform. Led by Muhammad Bulbulia, they rely on a robust pace attack and hard-hitting batting. The captain is the anchor of the batting lineup. His half-century in the warm-up against Sri Lanka showed he has the measure of their bowling. Corne Botha is the spearhead of the bowling attack. On the Bulawayo tracks, which can offer some early bounce, his opening spells will be crucial. Sri Lanka - The young Lions are captained by Vimath Dinsara, a technically sound batter, who is a crucial cog in the wheel for his side. Sri Lanka bring a tactical game centered around their high-quality spin department and nimble middle-order accumulators. Someone like a Viran Chamuditha is a genuine match-winner. He starred in the previous meeting with a gritty 87 and crucial wickets. His all-round capability makes him the MVP of this squad. What to expect - Historically, these two nations have shared a balanced rivalry at the U19 level, with South Africa holding a slight edge (10 wins to Sri Lanka’s 9). However, recent history favors the young Lions - in the tournament warm-ups earlier this January, Sri Lanka successfully defended 225 to beat the Proteas by 12 runs (DLS). This is a battle of contrasting styles. If South Africa’s top order can survive the initial spin trap and post a total north of 260, their pace battery might prove too hot for the Sri Lankan batters. However, if Sri Lanka can drag the Proteas into a spin-war on a tiring Bulawayo deck, they are the favorites to edge this contest. Who are you backing for the win?
